newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Over 50 wounded as strike grips Bangladesh port.
newsitem.headline: Over 50 wounded as strike grips Bangladesh port.

text.p: More than 50 people were wounded in bomb blasts, clashes and an attack on a train during an opposition-led general strike on Tuesday in Chittagong port and neighbouring areas, police said.
Activist supporters of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) exchanged gunfire and fought sporadic battles with supporters of the ruling Awami League, police said.
The BNP supporters ransacked railway offices, damaged a locomotive and attacked an Awami League office in Chittagong, witnesses said.
"More than 50 people have been injured in various incidents during the strike," a police officer in Chittagong said.
Opposition pickets barricaded tracks and attacked a train at Feni, 100 km (65 miles) from Chittagong, in which 15 people, including the train's driver, were injured, railway officials said.
But Deputy Inspector General of Police in Chittagong, Abdur Rahim, told reporters on Tuesday evening that "the hartal (strike) passed off without major violence".
Another police officer added: "We had feared a worse situation...but both sides showed some restraint."
BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia called for the dawn-to-dusk stoppage to protest what she said was "government-led terrorism and the ruling (Awami League) party's subservient policies towards India".
Khaleda has accused Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of being pro-Indian, jeopardising Bangladesh's national security.
Frequent bomb blasts shook the city and a number of vehicles carrying workers to the Chittagong Export Processing Zone were attacked and damaged, witnesss said.
Operations in the zone, which has 70 foreign industrial units, were badly affected with 80 percent of workers unable to report for duty, officials said.
Witnesses and officials said business came to a virtual standstill on Tuesday across southeast Bangladesh because of the daylong strike.
Trains, ferries and buses were halted, transport operators said. Air flights from Dhaka were running as normal, they said.
Chittagong Stock Exchange, commercial centres, industries, educational institutions, banks, and most government and private offices were closed.
Khaleda said she called the strike only in the greater Chittagong division because that was the area most affected by "government-led terrorism". She did not elaborate.
The BNP says the government has been persecuting political opponents, jailing thousands.
One senior BNP official said last week ruling party thugs had killed nearly 200 party workers and supporters since it came to power last June, a charge the government denies.
Khaleda said on Saturday that May 6 would "serve as a warning to this autocratic government and will be followed up, if necessary".
